transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Honestly, I’ve been taking on way too many projects at once and can’t seem to slow myself down at work or at home. It just feels like I'm constantly running on high gear and I can't find a way to stop.
Have you also been feeling unusually happy, irritable, or needing much less sleep than usual during this time?

Yes, I've definitely been experiencing that. I swing from feeling on top of the world, like a visionary who is going to reinvent corporate culture, to snapping at my team and feeling this white-hot anger over tiny things. I've also been sleeping significantly less, often staying up in the middle of the night to work on my projects.
How long have these episodes of high energy, mood swings, and reduced sleep lasted so far?
These problems have been going on for about a month now. It really started ramping up as the big corporate restructuring project at work took off.
Have you had any periods in the past where you felt this same way—very energetic, irritable or euphoric, and needing little sleep—that lasted at least four consecutive days?

No, I haven't really experienced anything this extreme or long-lasting in the past. This is the first time things have ever escalated to this level, especially with how intense it's been over the last month.
During this past month, have there been any days where your mood or energy level dropped significantly, such as feeling down, hopeless, or unable to function normally?
No, I haven't really experienced any low or down periods like that over this past month. My energy has stayed highly revved up the entire time, and I've just been constantly on the go.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, lost interest in activities, or had other symptoms like changes in appetite, sleep, or concentration before this current episode?

No, I don't recall ever having a period of two weeks where I felt persistently sad or lost interest in things. My struggles have always been more about being too revved up and taking on way too much, rather than feeling down.

The absence of a prior major depressive episode and the duration exceeding four days support a diagnosis within the bipolar spectrum. F31 (Bipolar affective disorder) remains appropriate as it encompasses various presentations of manic and mixed episodes, particularly given the ongoing nature of symptoms and no history of depression. No features suggest a psychotic or substance-induced disorder, and no other ICD-10 categories fit as well. However, the lack of prior episodes and absence of a clear depressive phase make it difficult to subtype further at this time.
